item.title: Uttar Pradesh Clears 20 MW Floating Solar Plant Project at Gorakhpur’s Chilua Tal
item.description: The Uttar Pradesh government has approved the installation of a 20 MW floating solar power plant at Chilua Tal in Gorakhpur, marking a step forward in expanding renewable energy capacity in the state. The decision was taken during a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday. item.title: KPI Green Energises 376 MWp RE Capacity, IPP Portfolio Reaches 965 MWp
item.description: KPI Green Energy Limited (KPI) has energised an additional 376 MWp (comprising ~182 MWp solar capacity in GUVNL 250/350 MWp project, ~164 MWp Solar capacity, and ~30 MWp Wind capacity in GUVNL 370 MW/677 MWp project). In a press release, KPI Green stated that it has now energised 965 MWp under its Independent Power Producer (IPP) portfolio, reflecting the phased development of its utility-scale renewable energy assets. item.title: Suzlon Secures 100 MW Wind Order From GAIL, Marks Sixth Project Partnership
item.description: Enhancing its strategic focus in the PSU segment, Pune-based Suzlon Group entered its sixth wind energy project of 100 MW from Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL). In a press release, Suzlon Group explained that this is Suzlon’s fourth PSU order of FY26, reflecting its growing strength in the ecosystem owing to its end-to-end capabilities. item.title: Vietnam Plans Two Renewable Energy Hubs by 2030 Under Revised JETP Roadmap
item.description: Vietnam has outlined plans to establish two renewable energy industry and service hubs by 2030 as part of its updated strategy under the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP). Under the revised plan, renewable energy is expected to account for approximately 47 percent of Vietnam’s total installed power capacity by 2030. item.description: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has stepped in to prevent 10.8 megawatts of wind capacity from being stranded, granting a time extension to a delayed project hit by heavy monsoon rains and equipment vandalism. item.title: Delhi Allocates Rs. 50 Cr For Rooftop Solar Under PM Surya Ghar Top-Up Scheme
item.description: The Delhi government has introduced the ‘PM Surya Ghar: Free Electricity Scheme – State Top-Up’, allocating a budget of Rs. 50 crore. Under this scheme, the government aims to equip 2.3 lakh residential rooftops with solar energy over the next three years. In her budget speech, Delhi Chief Minister (CM) Rekha Gupta shared that the goal of the latest budget is to provide uninterrupted and affordable electricity to every citizen of the capital. item.title: Beyond LFP: The Case for a Diversified Energy Storage Stack
item.description: In today’s battery landscape, it is easy to see why lithium-ion, specifically Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP), has become the undisputed leader in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). Plummeting costs and massive manufacturing scale-up have made LFP the bedrock of modern electrochemical energy storage. However, as renewable energy penetration deepens, the grid demands more. item.description: ReNew Energy Global Plc (ReNew) has agreed to sell its only commissioned project in Tamil Nadu—a 100 MW/117.5 MWp solar project—to the Technique Solaire Group for an enterprise value of $49 million. item.title: Rajasthan Adopts Central Renewable Consumption Norms, Scraps Separate RPO Targets
item.description: The Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission (RERC) has now attempted to align the state’s green energy compliance framework with the Union government's rules, issuing a suo-motu order to adopt the Centre’s Renewable Consumption Obligation (RCO) regime with immediate effect. item.description: Andhra Pradesh Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar has called on investors to accelerate the execution of renewable energy projects, stressing the importance of timely commissioning. item.title: UPNEDA Blacklists Rooftop Solar Vendor Under PM Surya Ghar, Forfeits Bank Guarantee
item.description: Uttar Pradesh’s renewable energy agency UPNEDA has blacklisted a registered rooftop solar vendor under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. The agency, however, did not publicly cite exact reasons behind the move but accused the firm of wrongdoings and working against the mandate of the renewable energy scheme.
